brief.headline: Push for a ₹28.69 L saving — we pay 33% more than Mars Plastics on our biggest cap, and we're nearly half their sales

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match our best prices on the three biggest items, starting with the 28 mm induction cap at ₹0.81/NOS
priceAsk.basis: We pay ₹1.08/NOS to them vs ₹0.81/NOS to Mars Plastics for the 28 mm PP cap (33.2% more), ₹1.53 vs ₹1.38 on the 30 ML bottle (10.7% more), and ₹0.46 vs ₹0.35 on the measuring cup (30.6% more). The market asks for a 28 mm induction cap sit at ₹0.55–1.20/pc, with typical at ₹0.85–0.95/pc — so our target of ₹0.81 is comfortably in-line and leaves them headroom.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 30 days instead of 45, in exchange for a price cut equal to half the cash we free up
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹8.01 L of our cash — ask them to split that benefit: they cut the price by about ₹4 L/year, we pay faster

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp is small — ₹4.11 Cr in sales — and we're ₹1.95 Cr of that, so 47.43% of everything they sell comes from us. They keep only 6.0% of each rupee they sell (similar firms keep 15.0%), so their profit cushion is thin. They already take 39 days to pay their own suppliers, longer than the 23 days typical for their peers, and their cash is tied up for 101 days (just under the peer 107 days). They borrow at around 4.54% to 8%, and they owe 1.13 times their own cash. All that means they need our volume badly and will value faster payment, but we should avoid a squeeze that could break them — their Altman score is 1.83 (grey zone). Lead with price to our best level and offer faster pay as a trade, not a hard push on both at once.

brief.suggestedOpeningLine: You're a key partner — nearly half your sales — so let's talk about how we bring your pricing in line with what we pay Mars and Premier, and how paying you faster can help both of us.
